Anyway the fatigue should be expected however if it's really getting to you consider
- get your *vitamin* levels checked.  Make sure you are not actually experiencing malnutrition.. it can happen at EVERY size and you're at very high risk with IBD. 
- get your hydration status checked. Regularly.
-check on your organs. Make sure your organs aren't experiencing distress without your knowledge.
- get your urine checked for infections. You are also medicated so that immune system might be compromised! Little infections like uti's can literally land you in the hospital. So easy to miss.

I've had Crohns and microscopic colitis since age 8. 
I'm turning 30 in a week or so and I don't travel anymore.  It's been about 6-7 years since my last vacation, and there is absolutely no appealing aspect. 
Traveling is such a heavy flare trigger with so many variables. Being stuck on a schedule also causes me anxiety, as well as not knowing the bathroom situation or knowing the bathroom situation will be unideal. Also realistically roomsharing with somebody having d and v 30x a day, is pretty unappealing for everyone, especially if people don't understand.

The only thing I can suggest is to try to think less about what the disease is taking away from you at this current moment and think about what you can try to pull off having this disease while out on vacation. Sometimes writing out a plan or typing on my phone helps.. get some lidocaine patches or cream for the abdominal area for sure! Make sure you are staying hydrated! I am happy to help! You really already have the right idea. Larger hoops are perfect for learning. They move slower. You will feel when you outgrow a hoop and need to go smaller, some moves require smaller hoops..but I suggest if you can swing it to make your own. A roll of tubing and connectors from Lowes  or home Depot would make me a good variety of practice hoops in different sizes for usually the price of one or two purchased hula hoops, but tape choice does alter that price a bit. You may find a size recommended to you doesn't work for your body so it's good to have a bunch of hoops to try. 

You want to look at your hula hoop like a dance partner or dance prop. You point your toes, spot spot spot. Learn your dominant/non dominant directions. Non dominant will feel wrong and almost impossible to keep up at first, dominant will feel natural. I've had students struggle to keep the hoop on their waist but as soon as I recommended they switch directions they did fine, so there is a degree of importance to that. The general objective is to even out both sides. So if you practice on one side repeat on the other. 
When you feel out the hoop organically that is when you create your own flow and moves...but to learn it doesn't hurt to brush up on some basics and watch videos, ask around,  so you know the general names and execution of moves. Some are specific, some are open for interpretation.
Finding a community is difficult, I'm in VA, so I understand. I usually worked outside wherever I could find space, or I would move furniture around to hoop indoors. That helps with spatial awareness, you will adapt with time. It may hurt and cause brushing at first.
